title: These Tadpoles Eat One Shrimp and Turn Into Cannibals

scenes.text: One meal turns these tadpoles into cannibals.
Spadefoot toads spend months buried in the desert, sometimes a year or two. When rain finally comes, they lay their eggs in puddles.
The puddle is already drying. The tadpoles have as little as a week or two to grow legs and get out.
Most are placid plant eaters. But if a young one eats a fairy shrimp, or another tadpole, its body rebuilds itself.
Its jaw muscles balloon. A sharp beak grows. Its gut shortens for meat. Then it starts hunting the other tadpoles in the pool.
In a shrinking puddle, the richest food left is each other. For almost a century, biologists thought the cannibals were a different species.

description:
Spadefoot toad tadpoles hatch in desert rain pools that can dry up within a couple of weeks. Most eat plants, but a tadpole that eats fairy shrimp or another tadpole early in life can switch into a carnivore form.
The carnivore grows a bigger head with swollen jaw muscles, a sharp keratin beak and a shorter gut, and it actively hunts other spadefoot tadpoles. The adults spend months, sometimes a year or two, buried underground waiting for rain.
Would you call that survival or horror?

first_comment: One spadefoot species can go from egg to land in about a week. What other animal changes its body to survive?
